# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 16: Anthropic Goes Public Today, With $900.9B of Spending Promised


### Anthropic starts trading today with $900.9 billion of spending committed, our first Throughput Thursday prices AI per task, Nvidia’s Data Center sales double, and Washington licenses AI cluster rentals.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 19, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/59PlJdmX3NUXWknmvej3my) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/ZwiEsVPv3ek) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week:


**Anthropic** starts trading on Nasdaq, priced above its range, with a filing that commits it to


**$900.9 billion** of future spending. The company that sells tokens by the million is going public by the trillion. Our first


**Throughput Thursday** prices the top models per task instead of per token.


**Nvidia’s** Data Center sales more than doubled; somebody’s been shopping. A new


**US rule** puts a license on renting big AI clusters to Chinese companies; the clouds will need to see your ID. And the Department of Token Efficiency has three cuts, from


**Perplexity** ,


**OpenClaw** and


**PostHog** . Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## Throughput Thursday


Our first one. Be gentle. It’s a baby.


Throughput is how much work a dollar buys, so we price it


**per task** . Price per token is the sticker. Price per task is the out-the-door price. Miles per gallon, if the car also wrote your emails.


[Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models) is an independent tester. Its Intelligence Index gives every model on its board the same


**nine** tests, from coding to science (


[methodology](https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking) ), and adds up the bill. Wednesday’s numbers:


Score vs dollars per task, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Wednesday 18 November.


-


**Claude Fable 5.2** (Anthropic): index score 65,


**$26.54** a task


-


**GPT-6.2 Astra** (OpenAI): 62,


**$4.00** a task


-


**GPT-6.2 Sol** (OpenAI): 57,


**$1.01** a task


-


**Claude Sonnet 5.5** (Anthropic): 54.5,


**$10.02** a task


-


**Fable** scores highest, a couple of points above Astra, but its task costs


**6.6 times** as much. More score, for more money. Extra credit, at private-school prices.


-


**Sol** is the bargain: a task costs about a dollar. Astra’s little sibling works for pocket change.


-


**Sonnet 5.5** is the opposite: about


**10 times** Sol’s price, for a lower score. A downgrade with a premium.


-


On


**December 1** , Google doubles what


**Gemini 4 Carbon** charges per token, from $2 to $4 per million input tokens and $10 to $20 per million output (


[Google pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) ). Artificial Analysis puts Carbon at


**$7.76** a task at the new price, almost twice Astra. Pay by the token, and you pay more for the same answers. Sticker shock, now with a delivery date.


**The catch.** A price per task assumes the task gets done once. Developer Matt Shumer posted that he gave Astra a job as a sub-agent, and Anthropic’s top models ended up redoing the work:


[Matt Shumer @mattshumer_ @JosttenSackitey Fable 5.2, some Opus 5.5. I even tried using 6.2 Astra as a sub-agent, but Opus/Fable got so frustrated with it and ended up redoing all the work themselves lol 6:16 PM · Nov 17, 2026 · 36.9K Views 13 Replies · 3 Reposts · 218 Likes](https://x.com/mattshumer_/status/2122755823806079145)


That’s one post. Another developer posted that Astra nailed his:


[Matt @MrCollison This is just wrong. I just tried GPT-6.2 Astra. Here's a 1 shot result trying to improve a game scene My prompt: "The NPC in this sequence feels fake. Please make him do realistic gestures that you would see when people speak in real life & any other improvements" It nailed it:… 8:25 PM · Nov 17, 2026 · 104K Views 129 Replies · 26 Reposts · 1.09K Likes](https://x.com/MrCollison/status/2122788211735048348)


If Fable redid it, you paid for the task twice:


**$4.00 + $26.54 = about $30.54** for one task, our estimate. You hired a babysitter, then stayed home anyway. So we stick to a named test. Tweets are vibes.


*Per-dollar verdict: dollars per task only counts if the task stays done.*


---


## The news: Anthropic goes public


Anthropic starts trading on Nasdaq today, at the 9:30am ET open, under the letters


**ANT** . It priced above its


**$70 to $78** range, at


**$83 a share** , and upsized the deal to


**980 million shares** , up from


**825 million** (


[Anthropic’s pricing release](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-prices-initial-public-offering) ;


[roadshow launch](https://www.anthropic.com/news/roadshow-launch) ). At that price, the offering raises


**$81.34 billion** , before the underwriters’ option for extra shares.


SpaceX’s June IPO came to


**$75 billion** on that same basis, by our math on the numbers in SpaceX’s filing (555.6 million base shares at $135; about


**$86.25 billion** with the extra shares) (


[SpaceX 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026043288/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm) ). Anthropic just passed it, on the same basis. Even IPOs get a leaderboard now. Wall Street finally gets to buy in. Usage limits not included.


**The bill behind the ticker.** Anthropic’s filing says it has committed to


**$900.9 billion** of future spending, nearly all of it compute and infrastructure. At the end of October, its revenue was running at about


**$81 billion a year** (


[S-1/A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026074338/anthropicpbc-sx1ax3.htm) ). So that spending bill is about


**11 years of revenue** at that pace. Most of us call that a mortgage. Then a second mortgage.


Agents need an office, and that’s where our landlords, the clouds, come in. Anthropic has signed a very long lease.


*Per-dollar verdict: Anthropic gets a ticker. You still get the invoice.*


---


## Nvidia’s quarter


Nvidia reported its third quarter on Tuesday (


[Nvidia](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx) ):


-


Revenue was


**$115.8 billion** , up


**103%** from a year ago.


-


**Data Center** sales did most of that, more than doubling to


**$107.6 billion** .


-


It beat its own forecast of


**$108 billion** . Nice work, if you get to write the test.


-


Revenue works out to about


**$1.27 billion every day** of the quarter, our estimate. Even the Sundays were billable.


-


Next quarter, Nvidia forecasts


**$130 billion** , give or take 3%. That includes an extra week, and assumes no Data Center sales to China. The quarter comes in an extended edition.


*Per-dollar verdict: every dollar of that was somebody’s line item. Possibly yours.*


---


## A new rule from Washington


A new US Commerce Department rule,


*Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors* , is out this week (


[Federal Register, public inspection](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/raw_text/202/623/529.txt) ); it takes effect on publication. Any data center, anywhere, now needs a US license to rent large amounts of advanced chips to companies headquartered in China. Same for Macau and other restricted countries. Turns out the cloud has borders.


-


Data centers already doing it have


**90 days** to get licensed.


-


The rule also adds license requirements for


**Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil** .


-


It ends the Biden-era


**AI Diffusion Rule** . One rule out, one license in.


*Per-dollar verdict: paperwork never shows up as a discount.*


All this to drive a future filled with


**Sticker-priced Intelligence** .


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Chainsaw fueled. Spreadsheets open.


**Cut one: Perplexity.** Aravind Srinivas runs Perplexity. On Monday he told Semafor its own fast-search model now serves


**80 to 90%** of its fast-search traffic, and that it saves


**$100 to $200 million a year** , at least (


[interview transcript](https://ceointerviews.ai/interview/3308935/) ). Perplexity mostly stopped ordering out and started cooking.


By his numbers, a dollar of revenue cost Perplexity


**$3.19** to serve at the end of 2025 (a gross margin of -219%). He says that by the third quarter of 2026 it kept


**17 cents** of each dollar, counting free users. Seventeen cents. Somebody frame the first one.


**The fine print:** it’s the CEO’s spoken claim, unaudited, and no detailed financials were released. Gross margin is not profit.


**Cut two: OpenClaw’s test machines.** OpenClaw’s coding agents were flooding its test machines. Free refills, and the robots noticed. Machine-hours fell


**86.5%** , from a peak week in September to a week in November. At published prices, its test machines would have cost


**$1.27 million** a month; now it’s about


**$57,000** ,


**95.5%** less (


[OpenClaw’s write-up](https://vincent.build/openclaw-ci-cost-reduction/) ). The robots got house rules.


**The fine print:** the sponsor covered those machines, so OpenClaw never paid these dollars. They’re estimates at published prices, the before is a peak week, and the workload changed. And it’s test machines.


**Cut three: PostHog’s gatekeeper.** PostHog’s privacy scrubber asks two yes-or-no questions with a decision model. Then


**98.7%** of summaries skip the AI call entirely (


[PostHog](https://newsletter.posthog.com/p/decision-models) ). Two questions, and the job goes home. Best meeting ever held.


**The fine print:** PostHog gave no dollar figure. It’s one pipeline. And in another project, a model update shifted the thresholds, so the team had to recalibrate.


The cheapest call is the one you never make.
